subject: OpenLine SLO probe & token-flow snapshot — post-demo next steps
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Teng <alex.teng@openline.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0500
Subject: OpenLine SLO probe & token-flow snapshot — post-demo next steps

Alex — thanks again for the demo today. Quick written recap so we have a single reference and clear next steps. I captured the approximations you gave on the call and highlighted the items we need to size the pilot reliably.

High-level workload notes (from call):
- Primary flow: real-time voice->ASR->LLM summarization and short-form convo memory.
- Average request: ~180 tokens (response tokens), median session length ~12s.
- Sustained baseline QPS you mentioned: ~6 QPS. Crest peak during promo windows: ~18 QPS (30–45s windows).
- Concurrent sessions: ~120 simultaneous streaming sessions (clients maintain bi-directional stream).
- Latency targets: p50 ~120–200ms, p95 <= 400ms per response chunk (tight for UX).
- Streaming requirement: partial token patches every ~200–300ms for first-word latency.

Immediate asks we still need from you:
1) Token histogram or sample distribution (tokens per request across 7 days) — helps pick batching/quantization profile.
2) A 5–10 minute session capture (raw events) for typical streaming session (client->server timing).
3) Expected KV cache reuse (percent of repeated context per session) — if you have an estimate for prefix reuse/hits.

What Redwood will do next:
- Run a conservative back-of-envelope sizing (tokens/sec and GPU-second estimate) based on the numbers above and any log samples you send.
- Map those to SLO choices (canary throughput, steady vs crest runway, streaming chunk targets).
- Propose a minimal pilot node shape and a test plan (latency assertions, load window script).

Proposed next step: short follow-up 30 min sync next Tuesday (Nov 24) to review the sizing sketch and decide pilot node shape. If you can get the sample logs and a small CSV of token counts per request that would be ideal — I attached an example session_sample JSON and a quick spreadsheet template for the token histogram.

Attachments: openline_session_sample.json (example), initial-throughput-notes.xlsx (histogram template).

Thanks,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0221

From: Alex Teng <alex.teng@openline.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: OpenLine Eng Team <eng@openline.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 17:05:12 -0500
Subject: Re: OpenLine SLO probe & token-flow snapshot — post-demo next steps

Naomi — great summary, thanks. A few clarifications from our logs that matter for sizing:
- Crest QPS: our peak crest can hit ~22 QPS for ~20–40s slices (weekend promos). We should size for that crest as a burst runway.
- Sustained: 4–7 QPS depending on region; EU is lower right now.
- Tokens: average response tokens are closer to 220 on longer sessions; median still ~160 for short interactions.
- Concurrency: on a heavy day we’ve observed ~150 simultaneous streams for the US region.
- KV reuse: roughly 25–30% reuse (we do short-term context windowing + user history lookup).

Attached: ol_session_logs_20261118.log (sample raw events), I exported a quick token_count.csv to the Drive folder linked below.

We can do the Tuesday slot — 11/24 10:00 PT works for us. I shared a Drive folder with raw artifacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1OpenLinePilotData

Thanks — Alex
Alex Teng
Senior Eng Manager, OpenLine
alex.teng@openline.ai

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 19:30:00 -0500
Subject: Fwd: OpenLine SLO probe & token-flow snapshot — post-demo next steps

Team — forwarding Alex's clarifications and sample log pointer. Key numbers to bake into a quick sizing sketch (BOE):
- Use crest QPS 22 for ~40s windows, sustained 6 QPS baseline (we'll model 4–8 QPS band).
- Average response token assumption: 220 (use median 160 and mean 220 scenarios).
- Concurrency: plan for 150 simultaneous streaming sessions (US).
- KV cache reuse: 25% (affects per-token compute if cache hits bypass attention for prefix).

Requests for the back-of-envelope run:
1) Rough tokens/sec calc for crest and sustained (two scenarios).
2) Estimate effective GPU throughput (tokens/sec) for a candidate model: open-approx 7B LLM with gpt-like decoder — include streaming chunk latency impact.
3) Quick node recommendation (pilot): start small but with headroom for crest (node type and number).
4) Confirm that partial-token emit every 200ms is achievable with the chosen kernel path (we'll validate with benchmark).

I'm happy to pair on the 30-min sketch. If either of you can kick off the BOE in a doc and drop numbers by EOD tomorrow that would be great. I'll own the meeting invite and notes.

— Naomi
